uncertainties: Lusatian-Pomeranian culture assigned to the 'baltic' family; its linguistic affiliation (para-Baltic vs pre-Germanic) is genuinely unresolved.

SIC is one region: assigned to the Greek side (greek_poleis, then Syracuse) every slice despite the Punic west; flagged contested throughout. At -400 Carthage actually held more area (post-405 treaty).
AND coast credited to Carthage from -500 after Tartessos' fall: Punic emporia (Gadir, Malaka) with Turdetanian interior.
CYR under Persia at -500/-480 (tributary after Cambyses, per Herodotus); independent Cyrene entity otherwise.
HUN sequence: Vekerzug 'Scythians' to -431, Pannonian Illyrians -400..-323, Celts by -301 - all approximations of a poorly documented plain.
COR: Etruscan sphere to -431 (post-Alalia), then loose Punic sphere from -400; no power firmly held Corsica.
PEL at -359 given to greek_poleis: post-Leuctra fragmentation (free Messene, Arcadian League) rather than Spartan control.
-323: CAP+PON given to Ariarathes I of Cappadocia (unconquered by Alexander); PON's inclusion is a stretch of his realm northward.

-301 details: CIL under Cassander's brother Pleistarchus (short-lived); CYP and the Cyclades kept by Demetrius contra a clean four-way split (brief's shorthand gave CYP to Ptolemy - Ptolemy only retook it -294); LEV de facto Ptolemaic though assigned to Seleucus at Ipsus - contested on both.
ARM/ARM_W at -323 nominally in Alexander's empire but Orontid de facto (kingdom from -321); at -301 ARM_W follows the brief to Seleucus.
Ireland labelled 'gaels' from -550; the date of Celticization is debated (possibly centuries later).
Odrysian interior (BGR) shown autonomous under Seuthes III at -323/-301 while Lysimachus holds the coasts (THR).
MDA: Scythian to -334 (Ateas' realm reached the Danube), Getic from -323 (Dromichaetes).
Population figures follow McEvedy & Jones low estimates (Achaemenid ~17-18M); other scholarship runs to 30M+.
